latest.text:
Fritz beat Musetti 6–4, 6–2 in the SF to reach the final and the head to head now stands at Fritz 4, Musetti 5. It was a one-sided match that lasted only 63 minutes.

Fritz played with aggression from the start and stepped in to take the ball early, which brought the key break in the third game for 2–1. He served very well after that and kept Musetti under pressure until the end of the set. It was the same story in the second set. Fritz was 0–1 down but broke for 2–1 at his second break point in that game, then won 5 games in a row and broke again for 4–1 on the way to 6–2.

He won it with a clear plan. Fritz lost only 9 points on serve in the whole match and did most of his damage with the forehand once the rally started. He also won 67% of the points against the second serve, compared with his usual 53%, so Musetti was never comfortable on his own serve either. On what he changed, Fritz said: "But the short answer is I just was a lot more aggressive and took on a lot more shots that are a bit uncomfortable for me. But I felt like against him, I have to if I wanted to win."

Musetti, a counterpuncher, had no answer to that attack and could not defend his way back into the match. He saved only 1 of 4 break points.

All in all, a dominant win from Fritz, built on his serve, his forehand and a plan he followed from the first game to the last and that mix of big serving and complete baseline play makes him very dangerous. He has not dropped a set this week and reached his sixth final of the year. Next is Tirante, who beat Munar in straight sets, needed three sets against Shevchenko in the QF and then beat Tabilo in straight sets in the SF.

latest.text:
Tirante beat Tabilo 7–5, 7–6 in the SF to reach his first tour-level final at his third attempt, which brings the head to head to Tirante 1, Tabilo 2. It was a tight match between two attacking baseliners, decided by one break in the first set and a tiebreak in the second.

Tirante started very strong on serve and lost just one point in his first service games. A single break decided the first set: Tirante broke for 6–5, faced 3 break points when he served for the set and saved all 3 to hold for 7–5. The first set could easily have gone the other way. In the second set he broke for 5–4 but nerves got to him when he served for the match and Tabilo broke straight back for 5–5. On that game, Tirante said: "Well, always we have nervous all the matches … I think I keep believing in me, in my team". He stayed with it and won the tiebreak and he has now played 4 tiebreaks this week.

The serve won it for him. Tirante won 90% of his first-serve points (!!!) and Tabilo could do very little against it. He also moved forward at the earliest chance and his net play was excellent. Most of his winners came from the forehand. He knows it himself: "With the forehand and with the serve there is a very danger for them."

Tabilo showed good touch and used the whole court. At times his shot choices were unclear and some of his volleys were not good enough to win the point. His forehand was not reliable, with 15 unforced errors on that side.

Physically, Tirante is something to follow. He called the physio early in the second set, his second medical timeout in two matches. We do not know the reason yet.

All in all, a tight win from Tirante, built on his serve and his attacking game at the net. It is already his second medical timeout this week, so his body is something to follow. Next is Fritz, who has not dropped a set this week: he beat Norrie in straight sets, got a walkover from Rune in the QF and then beat Musetti in straight sets.

latest.text:
Musetti beat Humbert 7–6, 3–6, 6–4 in the QF in their first meeting. It was a long fight of 2h29 between an attacker and a defender, with Musetti coming back from a break down in the deciding set.

The first set lasted about an hour without a single break of serve. Musetti saved 1 break point to hold for 3–2 and then won the tiebreak, in a set that could easily have gone the other way. He saved 2 more break points to hold for 1–1 in the second set but Humbert broke for 4–2 and took it 6–3.

The moment of the match came at the start of the third set, when Humbert broke for 1–0 and Musetti broke straight back for 1–1. Musetti said it simply: "The reaction was the key". Humbert saved 2 break points to hold for 2–2 and stayed with him until the very end, when Musetti broke for 6–4 to win the match, with an outstanding lob bringing up match point.

Musetti won it with his defence. He stayed deep behind the baseline, sent back almost everything Humbert hit and still found winners when he had the chance, 9 of them off the backhand.

Humbert attacked throughout, hitting the ball very hard at times and mixing in a delicate change of pace. His first serve let him down, though: he won only 69% of the points behind it, far below his 77% average on hard. That made the difference in the end.

Musetti did not look 100%. He called the physio early in the second set. Musetti after the match: "It's been a tough year for all the injuries, but now finally getting back in a good shape, so happy for that."

All in all, a patient win from Musetti, built on the defence and counterpunching that worked well on the medium-paced indoor court in Stockholm. His early medical timeout and the strapping under his right knee are things to follow. Next is Fritz, who has not dropped a set this week, beat Norrie in straight sets and then did not play his QF after a walkover from Rune.

Next is Fritz, who has not dropped a set this week, beat Norrie in straight sets and then did not play his QF after a walkover from Rune.
